transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Um, hi. Well... I guess I'm having some trouble with my eating. It's hard to explain, but... once I start, especially if I'm just alone in the kitchen, it's like I can't make myself stop. It kind of scares me, to be honest. It feels like I've just stepped aside, and even though I'm telling myself the whole time, 'Janet, put it away,' I just... I can't. So... that's why I'm here.
Can you describe what happens when you feel like you can't stop eating? Do you feel like you're losing control over how much you eat or how often you eat during those times?

Um... well, like I was just saying, it's... I guess it is exactly that. I just lose control over the amount. My brain is right there, telling me to stop, but... I just keep going. I don't really know how else to explain it.
After these episodes of eating, do you ever make yourself vomit, use laxatives, or exercise excessively to try to control your weight or shape?
No, I don't do any of that. I just... feel bad about it afterwards. But I don't throw up or anything.
Do you find yourself eating a lot more food than most people would in a short period of time, like within a couple of hours, even if you weren't really hungry?

Um... yes. I suppose I do. Like... sometimes after my shift at the food bank, or if I've been baking for the senior center... I'll come home and just eat. Even if I'm not really hungry. 

I'll have a full plate of leftovers, and then... I don't know, slices of banana bread. Chips. Cheese. Just... whatever cookies are in the tin. It's... well, when I think about it later, I realize it's way more than I would ever serve to another person.
Do these episodes of eating more than you intend cause you a lot of distress or interfere with your daily life in any way?

Um... I suppose it bothers me, yes. I mean, I still show up for my volunteer shifts, and... my craft fairs. I haven't stopped doing any of that. 

But... well, I've started skipping some of the shared meals we have afterwards. I just... I get embarrassed, I guess. And I don't really want people asking me why I seem upset. So I just avoid it.
During these times when you're eating more than you intend to, do you feel like you've completely lost control, like you can't stop eating even if you want to?

Yes... I do. That's... that's the part that really bothers me. 

Once I start, especially if I'm just alone in the kitchen... it's like I'm not even the one doing it anymore. I'll be standing there, and in my head, I'm thinking, 'Janet, just put it away.' But... I just can't make myself stop.
How often do these episodes happen? Do they happen at least once a week?

I... well, yes. I suppose so. If I look back at my kitchen calendar... and the weeks I'm at the food bank... it's probably happening most weeks. Maybe... once or twice a week. And it's been like that for... for many months now, I think.
During these episodes, do you find yourself eating much more rapidly than normal, like eating quickly without really thinking about it?

Um... yes. I suppose I do. 

I don't really think about it while it's happening, but... I catch myself eating so fast. I'll just be standing at the counter, taking bite after bite. I barely even taste the... the casserole or the muffins I made. It's just like I'm in a hurry, even when there's nowhere I need to be.
During these episodes, do you find yourself eating even until you feel uncomfortably full?
I... no, I don't think so. I haven't really noticed feeling like that, anyway.
Do you usually eat this way when you're alone, and if so, is it because you're uncomfortable eating in front of others?
I... well, I'm not really sure. I haven't really paid attention to whether I'm alone or not. I just... I don't know.
Can you recall if you're eating a very large amount of food in a short time, like within a couple of hours, even if it's not a scheduled mealtime?

I... I suppose so. Sometimes in the afternoon. Like if I get home from a shift at the food bank, or after baking for an event at the senior center... I'll just start eating. 

A full plate of leftovers, and then... some slices of banana bread, chips, some cheese. Just whatever cookies are in the tin. I don't really plan it, but... afterward I realize it was a lot. Way more than any meal I'd ever serve to another person.
Can you recall if you're eating a very large amount of food in a short time, even if you weren't really hungry?

I... yes, I suppose. A lot of times it's... well, after I've already had supper. My stomach isn't really asking for anything. But I still go back to the pantry or the fridge and... just keep picking at things. Until it turns into a lot, I guess.
Do you often find yourself eating large amounts of food even when you’re not really hungry?
I... yes. I think I just mentioned that. Like I said, it's usually after supper when my stomach isn't asking for it. I don't really know what else to add.
Do you usually eat this way when you're alone because you feel uncomfortable or distressed about eating in front of other people?
I... no, not really. I mean, I am alone when it happens, mostly, but... I don't think it's because I'm hiding. It's just when I happen to be by myself.
After these episodes of eating, do you often feel guilty, ashamed, or depressed about what you've done?

I... yes. Usually. Afterward, I just... I feel awful about myself. It's... well, I feel like I've wasted food that I was supposed to share with others. And I just think... I'm too old to be doing things like this. So I just sit there and... feel ashamed, I guess. I always tell myself it won't happen again.
